name: Regency gilded bone china
summary: Bone china with rich painting and heavy gilding for the houses of the Regency. The body has about 40 per cent bone ash, so it is strong, white and translucent, and it carries bold Imari patterns, botanical flowers and wide gold bands.

philosophy.core_thesis: Bone ash gives English potters a strong, white and warm body at a fair price, and they cover it in colour and gold to match the rich rooms of the Regency.
design_principles: Mix about 40 per cent calcined bone ash with china stone and kaolin for the body.
Fire the biscuit at 1250 °C and the glaze at about 1050 °C, so that the ware turns white and translucent.
Paint patterns in the Imari manner: dark blue under the glaze, then red and gold over it.
Paint flowers from botanical plates in the well of a dessert plate, one flower for each plate.
Gild the rim with a band 5 to 10 mm wide, and add a gold line round the foot.
Model the handles as leaves, scrolls or animal heads, and gild them.
Make a dessert service of 40 or more pieces, each with its own painted scene.
anti_patterns: A plain cream earthenware with a lead glaze
A thin pale pastel ground in the manner of Sèvres

form.shape: Dessert plates, dinner plates with a gilt rim, covered tureens, sauceboats, and footed dishes for fruit.
form.profile: A wide, round plate with a shaped or scalloped edge; the well is shallow, and the rim is broad for gold and colour.
form.foot_and_rim: A low foot with a glazed base; the rim is gilt, with a moulded scallop or a plain edge.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 21 to 24 cm and wall 2 to 3 mm thick; the gilt rim is up to 10 mm wide.
rules: Keep the wall thin, so that the plate shows light through it.
Divide the plate into a painted well and a gilt or patterned rim.
Gild all raised parts: the rim, the handles and the knop.

bodies.rule: Use a bone china body that is strong, white and translucent. Do not use earthenware: the style needs light to pass through the wall.

methods: slip casting of handles and knops
gilding with gold in honey or oil
burnishing the gold with a stone
forming.joins: Cast handles and knops are luted with slip; a lid sits in a rebated seat.
forming.details: Fine gilt lines, a pattern number painted in red in the base, and a polished gold band.

glaze.pattern: Imari patterns of blue, red and gold, botanical flower paintings, landscapes, and wide gold bands on the rim.
glaze.gloss: Bright gloss, about 85 to 95 GU, on a warm white ground.
glaze.wear: The gold wears at the rim and the handles; the glaze stays hard and keeps its shine.

palette.strategy: A warm white body, deep blue under the glaze, iron red and a heavy yellow gold over it.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle kiln; the biscuit is fired at the highest heat, then the glost, then the enamel and the gold.
firing.scale: Factories at Stoke, Derby, Worcester and Rockingham made services for the court and the new rich, and sold them to the world.
firing.signs: A pattern number in the base, a heavy gold rim, and a warm, translucent white.

pieces.form: Plate with an Imari pattern in blue, red and gold, and a gilt rim
Dessert plate with a botanical flower in the well and a wide gold rim
Covered tureen with leaf handles and a gilt knop, on a stand
Boat with a scroll handle and a band of gold lines

positive: Imari pattern in blue, red and gold

canonical_works.work: Rockingham dessert service for William IV

evidence.title: Tea service, Barr, Flight and Barr, Worcester, c. 1808

emotion.target_response: A rich, assured comfort: the viewer sees a heavy gold rim and a painted flower on a warm white plate, and thinks of a long dinner.

use_cases: a museum label on early bone china
avoid_when: the brief wants a plain or modern form
the brief wants a rustic matte glaze
the brief wants a cheap printed pattern

modifiers.how: Change the body to cream earthenware with a clear glaze and drop the gilt rim.
Keep the white body, drop the botanical painting, and use bands and angles in flat colour.
Replace the gilt band with a ground colour and white reserves, on a soft-paste body.
